newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ERTL SET TO MISS WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ERTL SET TO MISS WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Germany's Olympic silver medallist Martina Ertl injured her left knee in training for a World Cup Alpine skiing downhill on Thursday, almost certainly ending her world championship hopes.
Ertl, the women's World Cup giant slalom champion, crashed in Thursday's first training session and injured ligaments in her knee.
"She is going to Munich now and there the doctor will make a diagnosis," said team mate Katja Seizinger.
There was no official word on how long the 23-year-old athlete would be out of action but the nature of the injury made it unlikely that she would be back this season.
The world championships start in the Italian resort of Sestriere on February 2, the week after next.
Ertl, runner-up in the overall world Cup last season and 1994 Olympic giant slalom silver medlallist, won a giant bronze medal at the 1996 Sierra Nevada championships.
She had injured the same knee in October last year and needed a month to recover.
"(Martina) had the wrong line at the jump and then she flew in the wrong direction," said Seizinger, who had been unable to speak to her good friend and rival after the crash.
Cortina hosts a women's downhill on Friday. Thursday's training was the first after Tuesday's and Wednesday's sessions were called off due to snow and then fog.
